subject: science
intro: I'm Ms. Johnson. Let's plan a lab-based 7th grade lesson on identifying chemical reactions.

beats.narration: "New stuff" is the kid-friendly version of "new substances form."
beats.text: New Stuff: Evidence of Chemical Reactions

beats.narration: This standard asks students to analyze properties of substances before and after they interact.
The before/after comparison is the core of the standard.
beats.text: Students will be able to identify evidence of a chemical reaction by comparing the properties of substances before and after they interact.

beats.narration: Familiar objects make the idea concrete.
beats.text: Show a rusty nail next to a new nail, and a burnt marshmallow next to a fresh one. "Are these the same substance?" Discuss.

beats.narration: The physical change contrast prevents over-labeling everything as a reaction.
beats.text: Introduce the signs of a chemical reaction: gas, color change, temperature change, precipitate, and new smell. Contrast with physical changes (melting ice, dissolving sugar).

beats.narration: Including the melting ice tests whether they apply the criteria carefully.
beats.text: Lab stations: baking soda + vinegar, steel wool + vinegar, milk + vinegar, and ice melting. Students record properties before and after, then classify each as chemical or physical.

beats.narration: Two pieces of evidence reinforces careful observation.
beats.text: Pick one station. Was it a chemical reaction? Give two pieces of before/after evidence.

outro: Observe, define, test, explain. Now you plan.
